6743043894.name: mono - Share the Joy of New Finds
6743043894.description:
mono - An app for sharing the joy of welcoming new things home
mono is an app that lets you share your encounters with things, and the moment you bring them home, not just with yourself but with everyone.
By posting your everyday favorites and the collections you're proud of, you share that joy with other users and build a community.
By sharing the items you've "welcomed home" with other users, you can do more than just own things: you can cherish and enjoy the background and stories behind them.
Concept
Our lives are surrounded by things every day. Clothes, cosmetics, furniture, jewelry, stuffed animals, ornaments, and all sorts of other items add color to our lives. These items are not merely material objects; they carry emotions, memories, and even stories. mono treats this "welcoming home" of things as something special and provides a platform for sharing it with others.
Under the theme "Keep the joy of the moment you welcome something home, in photos and feelings," this app lets users share and enjoy with one another the excitement and joy that come from meeting new things.
mono aims not just for showing things off to each other, but for cherishing their background and stories and making the time spent with them richer.
Main features
Welcome-home posts
A feature for easily posting items you've newly brought home. Along with photos, you can share the item's name, features, where you bought it, and its story. Sharing the feelings and attention to detail you put into an item leads to deeper connections with other users.
Keep photos and stories
Photograph an item and post it with the stories and episodes that go with it. A souvenir bought on a trip, memories of a present from a friend, an item you welcomed home on a special day: you can convey not just the object, but the emotions behind it.
Favorite things corner
You can create a corner that gathers your most beloved items and show it to other users. In this corner, you can add a message along with photos that tells how much each item means to you.
Follow & comment
Follow other users to keep up with the items and posts that interest you. You can also use comments to share your impressions of, and empathy for, items others have welcomed home, and enjoy deeper interactions.
"Today's welcome" feed
A feed for sharing the items you welcomed home today, right away. By looking at other users' "Today's welcome," you can discover trends and new items and connect with people who share your hobbies.
Hashtag search
You can sort posts with hashtags like #WelcomedItems, #FavoriteItems, #Favorites, and #Matching. This makes it easy to search for posts about specific items or themes and share common interests with more people.
Stories for each item
For each item, you can keep a story about how you met it, what made you buy it, and what you thought after using it. This lets users not only show things to each other but also share the meaning and feelings they put into them, and find empathy.
Target audience
mono is developed for everyone who values their encounters with things and wants to share that joy and excitement. It especially targets women, and is ideal for people who enjoy sharing the things they treasure and their favorite items from daily life.
- People interested in fashion or interior design
- People who are proud of their collections
- People who treasure their memories
- People who keep up with new items and trends
- People who want to share their lifestyle with others
For these users, mono is a great fit as an app that offers heartwarming moments.
Design
The app uses a simple, refined, and beautiful design. Item photos take center stage, and to bring out their beauty, the background is based on calm pastel colors. The visually pleasant design lets users use the app comfortably and focus on the items that have been posted.
The user interface (UI) is also designed to be intuitive and easy to use, so even beginners can get started right away. It's a place to show each other the things you've welcomed home.
In closing
mono is a community app that values not just owning things, but your encounters with them, how they grow with you, and your attachment to them. While enjoying the memories of the items you've welcomed home and your connections with other users, you can make new discoveries and find empathy.
"Keep the joy of the moment you welcome something home, in photos and feelings": that is the essence of mono. Why not share the wonderful time you spend with your things, and connect over it with others?

6797057271.name: EyeMole - Eye Whack-a-Mole
6797057271.description:
No hands. Play with your eyes.

Your gaze is the hammer.

EyeMole is whack-a-mole you play with your eyes only. The front camera (Face ID / TrueDepth) tracks where you look. Stare at a mole for a split second and the hammer drops. No tapping. No swiping. Just looking.

THE DILEMMA
In EyeMole, looking is both how you check and how you attack. A chick sometimes pops out of a hole—and if you stare too long, you whack it and lose precious time. Glance, identify, and tear your eyes away. Your attention itself is the game.

THE CAST
- Mole: stare to whack. +100 and combo.
- Chick: don't stare! Whacking it costs you time. Spot it and look away for a bonus.
- Gold Mole: reads your gaze and pops up in your blind spot. Short-lived, big points.
- Flash Mole: a shiny decoy that yanks your reflexes. Worth nothing.
- Helmet Mole: a boss that shows up about 20 seconds into a round. Hold your gaze for 1.5 seconds for a big score—and letting it go won’t break your combo.

SCORE ATTACK
60 seconds per round. Chain correct decisions to build combos and beat your best. Compete on the Game Center world leaderboard—browsed and operated entirely by gaze, of course.

REQUIREMENTS
- iPhone or iPad that supports face tracking (Face ID devices, or iPads with A12 Bionic or later). This game cannot be played by touch.
- Camera permission. All face data is processed on your device—nothing is recorded, saved, or sent anywhere.
- A bright room and about 30–40 cm between you and the screen work best. A five-point calibration keeps your aim sharp.

Hearts limit play sessions (up to 3, one back every 10 minutes). Watch a short video to refill one instantly. EyeMole is free, supported by ads.

Your eyes have been training for this your whole life. Prove it.

6811730170.name: Bytebeat: Make Music with Code
6811730170.description:
t*(42&t>>10)

That one line is the whole song.

Bytebeat turns a formula straight into sound. It evaluates your expression while t counts up from zero, one step at a time, and writes the result out as the waveform. No synthesizer, no audio files, no samples. The formula is the music.

■ Edit while it plays
- Rewrite the formula without stopping playback. t keeps running
- Change a single character and the song becomes something else
- A keypad holding only the characters that appear in bytebeat formulas, so one tap is one character

■ See the waveform
- An oscilloscope draws the samples that are actually playing
- Traces are aligned to the rising edge, so the wave stays still instead of scrolling
- Instruction count and stack depth are shown too

■ 29 famous formulas
- Includes the one-liners from the experiments viznut published in 2011
- Save the ones you like to favorites with your own names

■ Three modes
- Bytebeat: result & 255 mapped to 0...255, the way the original sounded
- Signed: treated as signed 8-bit
- Floatbeat: the result used directly as a -1...1 waveform, where sin and cos come alive

■ Change the speed of t
- 500 to 48000 Hz. The original bytebeat ran at 8000 Hz
- Slower runs lower, faster runs higher

■ Export to WAV
- 8-bit, 8000 Hz, mono, which is exactly what bytebeat is
- 10 seconds, 30 seconds, 1 minute or 3 minutes

■ What you can write
- The variable t, and the constants PI and E
- Arithmetic, bitwise operators, shifts, comparison, logic, the ternary operator
- sin cos tan asin acos atan abs floor ceil round sqrt exp log sign int pow min max atan2 mod
- Everything is computed in Double and rounded to 32-bit integers only for bitwise operations and shifts. This matches JavaScript's ToInt32, so formulas you find on the web play as they are

■ No connection
- No account to create
- No ads, no tracking
- The app never connects to the internet. It works on a plane

Many of the presets come from the experiments Ville-Matias Heikkila (viznut) published in 2011.

6823032334.name: Tap Here: Phone Help with AI
6823032334.description:
"Where do I tap next?"
When you get stuck on your phone, just show a screenshot of that screen. Tap Here marks the place to tap with a red circle, a number, and an arrow.

Ask before you tap.
No more trying to explain "the gear icon at the top right…" over the phone.

HOW IT WORKS
1. Take a screenshot of the screen you are stuck on
2. Choose that screenshot in this app
3. Tap where the red circle is
You can also write what you want to do, such as "I want bigger text", for more detailed steps.

ONE STEP AT A TIME, READ ALOUD
- Steps are shown one by one. Tap "Next" to see the next place to tap
- Each step is read aloud (you can turn this off)
- Tap the screenshot to zoom in

CONTINUE ON THE NEXT SCREEN
When the screen changes, show a screenshot of the new screen. The app remembers what you want to do and continues from there.

CAUTION ON SUSPICIOUS SCREENS
Screens that ask for money or a PIN, or fake virus warnings, are marked with a "Caution" note. If you are not sure, ask your family before you tap.

SEND TO FAMILY
Send the picture with the circles to your family in a messaging app and talk it through together.

LOOK BACK AT PAST GUIDES
Guides are saved on your phone, and you can add memos.

EASY TO START

Only the English you actually use on a trip.

This is not an app for redoing school English. The airport counter, ordering at a restaurant, checking in at a hotel, asking for directions. Losing your wallet, breaking a large bill, checking out on the day you leave. We narrowed it down to 403 phrases you will really say out loud while traveling.

■ Learn the meaning directly, with pictures and voice
Every question comes with a picture. Instead of translating from Japanese into English, you tie the scene and the sound together as they are. All the voices are pre-recorded, so they play even without a connection.

■ 5 questions per stage
Each stage is short enough to finish in one breath. One stage on the train to work, or in the few minutes before bed. Even if you only have a few days until departure, you can make it.

■ Numbers, the hardest part of any trip
Prices, times, numbers, dates, booking codes. Thirteen and thirty, fourth and fourteenth, "double seven" — the things that really hurt when you cannot catch them, turned into listen-and-pick practice.

■ 60 pairs of similar sounds
Right and light, sea and she. The sounds Japanese speakers stumble on, trained into your ear with two-choice questions.

■ 96 signs you will see on the road
EXIT, NO ENTRY, KEEP LEFT, OUT OF ORDER. The signs actually standing in airports, stations, shops and hotels, in a list you can look up on the spot.

■ Travel cheat sheet
Every phrase is there whether you have memorized it or not. When you are stuck, open it and show it to the other person as is. Tap it and it reads the phrase aloud.

■ Turn their English into text
When you could not catch what they said, tap "Listen" and the other person's English shows up on screen as text.

■ Collect
64 titles and 36 badges. Weekly leagues let you compete casually with other people.

■ About your records
Your solving records are saved on this device. When you switch phones, export them from "Export records" inside the app and import them on the new device. Your name tag (name, look, rank) is tied to your Apple or Google account, so it carries over as is.

An ad may appear after you finish a stage. Ads never appear while you are solving questions. They also never appear on the screens you open when you are stuck on a trip: the travel cheat sheet, the signs, and the listen feature.
